- If sentiment is consistently neutral or flat, avoid over-optimistic forecasts; price tends to revert to mean or show muted momentum.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.0), model should slightly under-forecast to avoid over-shooting upward trends.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.0), model should slightly over-forecast to counteract downward pressure — but avoid excessive overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overreact in the short term; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >75% increase from recent 5-day avg), apply mean reversion bias — reduce forecast slope by 15–25%.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after forecast peak, model likely overestimated momentum — adjust next period downward by 5–10%.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–), model should smooth forecasts — avoid sharp directional jumps.
